```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
d <- fread("../output/cluster_characteristics.csv")
```

# Dataset Overview

**File:** `outputs/cluster_characteristics.csv`
**Unit of analysis:** URL cluster — a group of topically related URLs shared on Brazilian Facebook pages during the 2018 and 2022 electoral cycles.
**Rows:** `r nrow(d)` (`r d[year==2018,.N]` clusters in 2018, `r d[year==2022,.N]` in 2022)
**Columns:** `r ncol(d)`
**Missing values:** `weighted_mpas` and `mpas_abs` are `NA` for `r sum(is.na(d$weighted_mpas))` clusters with no domain matched in `proportions.csv`.

---

# Variables

## Identifiers

### `year`
**Type:** Integer
**Values:** 2018, 2022
Election cycle in which the cluster was observed.

### `cluster`
**Type:** Integer
**Values:** Unique within each year
Cluster identifier assigned by the k-means algorithm.

### `label`
**Type:** Character
Short descriptive label of the cluster's dominant topic, generated automatically from the top URLs and their content. Example: *"Haddad 2018 PT presidential campaign"*.

### `predicted_categories`
**Type:** Character
Automated content category with URL count in parentheses. Example: *"politics (812)"*. In this dataset all clusters are classified as `politics` — finer topic distinctions for RQ1a should be derived from `label` via manual or automated sub-categorisation.

### `topic`
**Type:** Character
Cleaned version of `predicted_categories` with the count removed. All values are `"politics"` in the current dataset.

---

## Temporal variables

### `date_start`
**Type:** Datetime (POSIX)
Timestamp of the first URL shared in the cluster.

### `date_end`
**Type:** Datetime (POSIX)
Timestamp of the last URL shared in the cluster.

### `duration_days`
**Type:** Numeric
**Range:** `r round(min(d$duration_days),1)` – `r round(max(d$duration_days),1)` days
**Mean:** `r round(mean(d$duration_days),1)` | **Median:** `r round(median(d$duration_days),1)`
Time span between `date_start` and `date_end`. Most clusters span close to the full electoral window (~90 days); shorter clusters reflect more episodic events.

```{r duration-plot, fig.height=3, fig.width=6}
ggplot(d, aes(x = duration_days, fill = factor(year))) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, colour = "white", alpha = 0.8, position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("2018" = "#4393c3", "2022" = "#d6604d")) +
  labs(x = "Duration (days)", y = "Clusters", fill = "Year") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

---

## Volume variables

### `total_urls`
**Type:** Integer
**Range:** `r min(d$total_urls)` – `r max(d$total_urls)` | **Median:** `r median(d$total_urls)`
Total number of unique URLs in the cluster, including links to social media platforms.

### `n_urls_no_social`
**Type:** Integer
**Range:** `r min(d$n_urls_no_social)` – `r max(d$n_urls_no_social)` | **Median:** `r median(d$n_urls_no_social)`
Unique URLs excluding social media platforms (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter/X, TikTok, and others). This is the base for ideology computation.

### `n_domains`
**Type:** Integer
**Range:** `r min(d$n_domains)` – `r max(d$n_domains)` | **Median:** `r median(d$n_domains)`
Number of unique `full_domain` values in the cluster, excluding social media.

---

## Ideology variables

### `weighted_mpas`
**Type:** Numeric
**Range:** `r round(min(d$weighted_mpas, na.rm=TRUE),3)` – `r round(max(d$weighted_mpas, na.rm=TRUE),3)` | **Mean:** `r round(mean(d$weighted_mpas, na.rm=TRUE),3)` | **Median:** `r round(median(d$weighted_mpas, na.rm=TRUE),3)`
**Missing:** `r sum(is.na(d$weighted_mpas))` clusters

URL-frequency-weighted mean of the MPAS scores (Santos 2023) of all domains in the cluster with a valid ideology score. Score ranges from −1 (far left) to +1 (far right). Computed from non-social-media URLs only.

**Formula:** $\text{weighted MPAS} = \frac{\sum_{d} \text{MPAS}_d \times n_d}{\sum_{d \in \text{matched}} n_d}$

where $n_d$ is the number of URLs from domain $d$ in the cluster.

```{r mpas-dist, fig.height=3, fig.width=6}
ggplot(d[!is.na(weighted_mpas)], aes(x = weighted_mpas, fill = factor(year))) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, colour = "white", alpha = 0.8, position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("2018" = "#4393c3", "2022" = "#d6604d")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Weighted MPAS", y = "Clusters", fill = "Year") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

### `mpas_abs`
**Type:** Numeric
**Range:** `r round(min(d$mpas_abs, na.rm=TRUE),3)` – `r round(max(d$mpas_abs, na.rm=TRUE),3)` | **Mean:** `r round(mean(d$mpas_abs, na.rm=TRUE),3)` | **Median:** `r round(median(d$mpas_abs, na.rm=TRUE),3)`
**Missing:** `r sum(is.na(d$mpas_abs))` clusters

Absolute value of `weighted_mpas`. Operationalises **partisan intensity** regardless of direction: clusters near 0 are centrist or mixed-source; clusters near 1 are strongly partisan (either left or right). Primary independent variable for RQ1.

### `n_matched_urls`
**Type:** Integer
**Range:** `r min(d$n_matched_urls)` – `r max(d$n_matched_urls)` | **Median:** `r median(d$n_matched_urls)`
Number of URLs (excluding social media) whose domain was matched in `proportions.csv`.

### `pct_matched_urls`
**Type:** Numeric (percentage)
**Range:** `r min(d$pct_matched_urls)`% – `r max(d$pct_matched_urls)`% | **Median:** `r median(d$pct_matched_urls)`%
Percentage of non-social-media URLs covered by the MPAS measure. Indicates reliability of `weighted_mpas`: a low value means the ideology score is based on a small fraction of the cluster's URLs.

### `n_matched_domains`
**Type:** Integer
**Range:** `r min(d$n_matched_domains)` – `r max(d$n_matched_domains)` | **Median:** `r median(d$n_matched_domains)`
Number of unique domains matched to an MPAS score.

### `pct_matched_domains`
**Type:** Numeric (percentage)
**Range:** `r min(d$pct_matched_domains)`% – `r max(d$pct_matched_domains)`% | **Median:** `r median(d$pct_matched_domains)`%
Percentage of unique domains (no social media) with a valid MPAS score.

---

## Structural variables

### `pct_social_media`
**Type:** Numeric (percentage)
**Range:** `r min(d$pct_social_media)`% – `r max(d$pct_social_media)`% | **Median:** `r median(d$pct_social_media)`%
Percentage of the cluster's total URLs (`total_urls`) that link to social media platforms. A high value indicates a cluster organised around social platform content rather than news outlets. Social media platforms carry no MPAS score and are excluded from ideology computation.

### `gini_domains`
**Type:** Numeric
**Range:** `r round(min(d$gini_domains),3)` – `r round(max(d$gini_domains),3)` | **Mean:** `r round(mean(d$gini_domains),3)` | **Median:** `r round(median(d$gini_domains),3)`
Gini index of URL concentration across domains within the cluster (computed on non-social-media URLs).

- **0** = perfectly even distribution across all domains
- **1** = all URLs concentrated in a single domain

A high Gini indicates the cluster is effectively a single-outlet community; a low Gini indicates a diverse multi-source audience. Useful as a validity check on `weighted_mpas` (high Gini + low `pct_matched_urls` means the dominant domain has no ideology score) and as a control variable in models.

---

## Cohesion variables

### `mean_cos_sim_to_centroid`
**Type:** Numeric
**Range:** `r round(min(d$mean_cos_sim_to_centroid),3)` – `r round(max(d$mean_cos_sim_to_centroid),3)` | **Mean:** `r round(mean(d$mean_cos_sim_to_centroid),3)` | **Median:** `r round(median(d$mean_cos_sim_to_centroid),3)`
Mean cosine similarity of all URL embeddings in the cluster to the cluster centroid. Measures **semantic cohesion**: how topically tight the cluster is. Higher values indicate URLs that are more consistently about the same topic.

### `median_cos_sim_to_centroid`
**Type:** Numeric
**Range:** `r round(min(d$median_cos_sim_to_centroid),3)` – `r round(max(d$median_cos_sim_to_centroid),3)`
Median version of the above. Less sensitive to outlier URLs with very low similarity.

---

# Notes for the Secure Environment

- Join to the URL-level engagement data on `year` + `cluster` (or via the `url_rid` → `year_cluster` mapping in `url_rid_year_cluster.csv`).
- `weighted_mpas` and `mpas_abs` are `NA` for `r sum(is.na(d$weighted_mpas))` clusters — exclude these from ideology models or treat as a separate "unclassified" category.
- For **RQ1a** (topic moderation): `predicted_categories` is uniformly `"politics"` and cannot serve as a moderator as-is. Topic sub-categories should be derived from manual coding or further automated classification of the `label` field.
- `pct_matched_urls` should be used as a **weight or filter** in models: clusters with very low coverage (e.g. < 20%) have unreliable `weighted_mpas` estimates.
